translations./beats/0/text: Backup power is back in the repair bay. RO-1 waits on the service stand.
translations./beats/1/text: Motion module online. Can you… hear me?
translations./beats/2/text: There is no route in memory. For now, I can only follow the direction you give me.
translations./beats/3/text: My wheels say I arrived, but the mark on the wall disagrees. Did I lose track of where I am?
translations./beats/4/text: The old route is blocked. I need to plan a new path from the map as it is now.
translations./beats/5/text: The power module is ready. The forklift is still patrolling; I’ll decide when it is safe to cross.
translations./beats/6/text: RO-1, if you receive this transmission, do not reboot the main controller.
translations./beats/7/text: When the signal tower came online, another echo answered from deep inside the depot. Let’s run it again with a different approach.
translations./beats/8/text: Same forklift. Same road. We’re the part that changed.
translations./beats/9/text: You never know if a pair of shoes fits until you run in them. You choose; I’ll drive.
translations./beats/10/text: So that’s what grip feels like—the braking point moved.
translations./beats/11/text: They say high-torque motors have strong personalities. Shall we try one?
translations./beats/12/text: It really is stronger. It really does draw more power.
translations./beats/13/text: We know every part now. Let’s take a longer run.
translations./beats/14/text: Working together feels better than the sum of the parts.
translations./beats/15/text: From the signal tower back to the calibration pad—the longest stretch yet. Let’s take it steady.
translations./beats/16/text: Home. The secret to a long haul is no secret at all: hold a steady speed.
translations./beats/17/text: Let’s send RO-3 up the northern route too.
translations./beats/18/text: Arrived. Same road, different feet—it feels completely different.
translations./beats/19/text: Let’s send RO-3 along the sandy route too.
translations./beats/20/text: Arrived. On sand, tracks and patience go together.
translations./beats/21/text: Let’s send RO-2 along the sandy route too.
translations./beats/22/text: Arrived. On sand, I have to steer before the turn.
translations./beats/23/text: Let’s have RO-3 skim the edge of the wet zone.
translations./beats/24/text: Made it through. When tracks churn water, slow is the only rudder.
translations./beats/25/text: This shift’s forklift is different. It blocks the route for several seconds. We win this one by waiting; otherwise, we only wait to get hit.
translations./beats/26/text: It passed. The corridor belongs to the forklift; we’re borrowing a few seconds.
translations./beats/27/text: Let’s send RO-3 through that old intersection where it used to oscillate.
translations./beats/28/text: Arrived. No oscillation this time. The watchdog remembers.
translations./beats/29/text: Same route, same traffic. Let’s try it with slower eyes.
translations./beats/30/text: The 5 Hz sensor fell behind at the east end of the corridor. Seeing more often means driving more precisely.
translations./beats/31/text: This route is different from the corridor: the forklift approaches from the side. We’ll let it pass.
translations./beats/32/text: It passed. You get through an intersection by yielding, not squeezing past.
translations./beats/33/text: We graduated! First town job. Traffic on Main Street, sand on the curve. Take it slow and arrive on time.
translations./beats/34/text: First delivery complete. The mayor says the town’s freight is ours from now on.
translations./beats/35/text: The big town! Five districts, three streets, and pedestrians. Take it slow; one delivery at a time.
translations./beats/36/text: Big town complete. Pedestrians are more reasonable than forklifts—yield to them and they yield to you.
